status: new draft two-copy reduction for the remaining primitive vertex obligation; full vertex theorem unresolved
new_source_before: absent; newly authored, no existing source overwritten
proved: A rational kernel perturbation of a non-extreme fundamental disk gives some nonproportional integer multiple sum.

At minimum multiplicity and then minimum double-curve count, connected proportional components cancel and disconnected summand families can be regularly absorbed to reduce the count. Hence both summands may be assumed connected.

Euler characteristic and unchanged boundary count for a closed summand force multiplicity exactly two. The only pairs are disk+disk or sphere+annulus, with annulus boundary the two essential copies of the disk boundary.
If the original disk is least-weight essential and lexicographically least, disk+disk cannot have both summands essential: weight and vector averaging would make both equal the original disk.
not_proved: The two-copy cases are impossible or give a primitive extreme-ray essential disk.
The general primitive vertex-disk existence theorem.
authentic_source_caution: The authentic JT paper Example3.2 explicitly gives a least-weight essential fundamental disk that is not a vertex. Its Theorem4.3 disk criterion has its proof omitted, and Cor6.4 assumes irreducibility. None is substituted for the remaining local proof.
